doc.name: A — power bank catalogue, frozen toss, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: GaN charger and braided cable
Category: power bank
Shot programme: frozen toss
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You run the tabletop stage for a premium power bank product shoot. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the shadow-play silhouette in a frozen toss treatment.

SUBJECT. A GaN charger and braided cable. Lock the product itself to the reference — no proportional drift, no invented branding, no cleaned-up typography. Everything else in the frame is your design decision.

CAMERA. Backlit so the product edge glows and the set falls into shadow. Shoot on a 35mm reportage at f/2.8, framing for rule-of-thirds weighting to frame-left with open air to the right.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with hard low sun raking across the surface with long cast shadows. Stage the product on or against raw board-formed concrete, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a punchy saturated candy palette with hard primaries. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. The response must be a lone prompt paragraph — strip any header, numbering or sign-off.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
